problem.lead: McKinsey has already named the problem and priced it:
problem.statement: The blind handoff — the moment two parties exchange goods and neither can see what the other is doing.

impact.title: The last few feet are the most expensive
impact.body: You've optimized routes, warehouses, and fleets. The handoff itself is where time, vehicles, and goods still go to waste.

metrics.body: Hours spent waiting at the handoff each year in US B2B delivery, plus 160M more in B2C.
metrics.veranda: An unattended endpoint means nobody waits for anybody.

metrics.body: US deliveries that fail on the first attempt — 1 in 9 simply because nobody was there.
metrics.veranda: The access point opens for a verified carrier, whether or not anyone is home.

metrics.body: Share of the 23 billion US parcels re-delivered each year, costing carriers 1–3% of revenue.
metrics.veranda: Completing the first attempt removes the second trip.

metrics.body: Share of US parcels lost or stolen after delivery.
metrics.veranda: Goods wait in a locked, logged enclosure — not on the doorstep.

metrics.body: Dispatcher and service time spent coordinating around handoff failures.
metrics.veranda: No driver app, no key, and no call-ahead needed to arrange access.

metrics.body: Lost carrier revenue from 1–1.5 avoidable hours per truck, per day.
metrics.veranda: Vehicles and crews spend their hours completing drops, not attempting them.

impact.note: Figures describe the US market as reported in industry research, including McKinsey & Company (cited above). They are not projected Veranda results.
